root_cause.text: The code used READ_ONCE() and WRITE_ONCE() on an 8-byte struct (`sysctl_fib_multipath_hash_seed`) that has only 4-byte alignment, causing ARM64 alignment faults (from `ldar` requiring natural alignment under Clang LTO) and non-atomic tear writes.
root_cause.evidence: CVE description states that `READ_ONCE()` on the full struct triggers a 64-bit `ldar` instruction on a 4-byte aligned address, causing an alignment fault (FSC=0x21). The patch fixes this by moving `READ_ONCE()` to the individual `u32` member and splitting `WRITE_ONCE()` into two separate 32-bit operations to avoid alignment and atomicity issues.

intent_record.intent_summary: Correct the use of READ_ONCE to apply to the member mp_seed instead of the entire struct to ensure atomic read of the seed value.
intent_record.what: Changed the assignment of mp_seed from READ_ONCE on the entire struct followed by member access to READ_ONCE directly on the member.
intent_record.how: Ensures atomic read of the mp_seed scalar field instead of potentially non-atomic read of the whole struct.

intent_record.intent_summary: Restrict multipath hash seed update to only the user_seed and mp_seed fields to avoid overwriting other struct members.
intent_record.what: Replaced a single WRITE_ONCE that wrote the entire new structure to net->ipv4.sysctl_fib_multipath_hash_seed with two WRITE_ONCE calls that write only the user_seed and mp_seed fields.
intent_record.how: Previously, writing the whole struct would overwrite all fields, potentially corrupting other state variables. Now only the two intended seed fields are updated, leaving other fields unchanged.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use READ_ONCE to safely read the seed value in the multipath hash seed sysctl handler, preventing potential data races from concurrent writes.
intent_record.what: Replaced direct read of mphs->user_seed with READ_ONCE(mphs->user_seed).
intent_record.how: Adds a compiler barrier and ensures the read of the field is atomic, preventing potential data races from concurrent modifications.

candidates.rationale: READ_ONCE on the 8-byte struct which has only 4-byte alignment causes ARM64 alignment faults (ldar requires natural alignment) and non-atomic read.
WRITE_ONCE on the 8-byte struct with 4-byte alignment causes non-atomic tear writes on architectures that require aligned stores.

WRITE_ONCE is applied to the 8-byte struct with 4-byte alignment, resulting in non-atomic tear writes on architectures that require aligned stores, such as ARM64.
